**If you pick "Cloud: ChatOpenAI":** **Cloud, paid per token.** Follows the three-part contract: one headline, exactly three bullets, one interview question. `response.content` is a list of blocks, so read `.text`.

**If you pick "Local: ChatOllama":** **Local, free and private.** Comes back fast, but a 270M-parameter model often ignores parts of the instructions: four bullets instead of three, or no interview question. `.content` is already a string; `.text` still works.

inserts.md:
- 1 · Your question goes to the model as a HumanMessage.
- 2 · The model replies with a tool call: search({'query': 'Bengaluru weather now'}).
- 3 · LangChain runs search() and sends back a ToolMessage with the result.
- 4 · No more tool calls, so the model writes the final answer. Done.

inserts.after: Ten quick questions. Pick an answer to see why it's right or wrong.
inserts.md:
**1. Why do the scripts load keys with load_dotenv() from a .env file?**

- It makes the model answer faster
- Keys stay out of the code and out of git, and every SDK reads them from environment variables
- OpenAI refuses keys typed into code
- It encrypts the keys

> **Correct answer:** Keys stay out of the code and out of git, and every SDK reads them from environment variables
> .env is listed in .gitignore, and load_dotenv() copies each KEY=value line into the environment, where OpenAI, Tavily and LangSmith look for their keys.

**2. What does prompt | llm create?**

- A Python list of two objects
- A RunnableSequence: the filled prompt flows into the model
- A shell pipe between two processes
- A second copy of the template

> **Correct answer:** A RunnableSequence: the filled prompt flows into the model
> The pipe operator (LCEL) joins runnables. chain.invoke({...}) runs the template first, then the model.

**3. To move Script 02 from OpenAI to a local Ollama model, what changes?**

- The prompt template
- The chain and invoke() call
- Only the model object: ChatOpenAI becomes ChatOllama
- Everything, local models need a different library for chains

> **Correct answer:** Only the model object: ChatOpenAI becomes ChatOllama
> Every LangChain chat model has the same interface, so the prompt, the chain and invoke() stay identical.

**4. Why does every script print response.text instead of response.content?**

- content is always empty
- On newer OpenAI models content can be a list of content blocks; text is always one plain string
- text is faster to compute
- content holds the prompt, not the answer

> **Correct answer:** On newer OpenAI models content can be a list of content blocks; text is always one plain string
> Through the Responses API, .content may be a list. .text works the same for every provider.

**5. Where do you find how many tokens a call used?**

- response.id
- response.tool_calls
- response.usage_metadata
- response.type

> **Correct answer:** response.usage_metadata
> usage_metadata holds input, output and total tokens in a provider-independent shape. That's your cost.

**6. With @tool, what does the model actually see about your function?**

- The full source code
- Its name, type hints (input schema) and docstring (description)
- Only the return value
- Nothing until it's called

> **Correct answer:** Its name, type hints (input schema) and docstring (description)
> That 'menu card' is all the model knows, which is why the docstring is written for the model.

**7. In the agent loop, who runs the search function?**

- The LLM, on OpenAI's servers
- LangChain, after the model requests it in a tool call
- Tavily decides when to run it
- The user, by pressing Enter

> **Correct answer:** LangChain, after the model requests it in a tool call
> The model only requests a call. LangChain executes the function and adds a ToolMessage with the result.

**8. The placeholder run prints 4 messages. What's the order?**

- Human, Tool, AI, AI
- AI, Human, Tool, AI
- Human, AI (tool call), Tool, AI (answer)
- Human, AI, AI, Tool

> **Correct answer:** Human, AI (tool call), Tool, AI (answer)
> Question, the model's tool request, the tool's result, then the final answer with no tool calls.

**9. What's the main gain from swapping your own Tavily wrapper for TavilySearch()?**

- It's the only way to search the web
- Less code to maintain and a richer menu card: the model can set time_range, topic, include_domains and more
- It doesn't need an API key
- It always returns exactly three results

> **Correct answer:** Less code to maintain and a richer menu card: the model can set time_range, topic, include_domains and more
> The vendor-maintained tool documents extra arguments, and the model used them on its own (time_range='month').

**10. When does LangChain use ToolStrategy for response_format?**

- Always
- When the model has no native structured output: it adds an extra 'answer' tool whose arguments are the schema
- Only with Tavily tools
- When the schema has no fields

> **Correct answer:** When the model has no native structured output: it adds an extra 'answer' tool whose arguments are the schema
> Providers with native support (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) get ProviderStrategy. Either way you read result["structured_response"].

> **Score 8 or more of 10:** Great work, you're ready for Lesson 1.
>
> **Score under 8:** Revisit the parts you missed, then try Lesson 1.

glossary.definition: A secret string that proves who you are to a service such as OpenAI or Tavily. Anyone holding it can spend your credits, so keep it out of code and screenshots.
A plain text file of KEY=value lines kept next to your code but listed in .gitignore, so secrets never reach git. load_dotenv() reads it.
A named value the operating system hands to every program it starts. SDKs read their keys from fixed names such as OPENAI_API_KEY.
A fast Python project tool. uv sync creates the virtual environment and installs the exact locked versions; uv run runs a command inside it.
A private folder of Python libraries for one project, so different projects don't clash over versions.
A prompt with {placeholders} that LangChain fills in at run time, so the same instructions work on any input.
A {name} in a template that gets replaced by real text when the chain runs. The keys you pass to invoke() must match.
A Python object that talks to an LLM, such as ChatOpenAI or ChatOllama. All of them share the same interface.
LangChain's common building block: anything you can .invoke(). Joining runnables with | makes a RunnableSequence.
LangChain Expression Language: building chains with the pipe operator, so the output of one block flows into the next.
A setting for how random the model's wording is. 0 asks for the most predictable answer.
A free app that downloads open-weights models and serves them on your own machine at localhost:11434. No key, no cost.
A model whose trained weights are published, so anyone can download and run it locally. Gemma, Qwen and Llama are examples.
The object a chat model returns: the answer (.text), raw content, tool_calls, usage_metadata, response_metadata and an id.
The unit LLMs read and write: roughly three-quarters of an English word. Prices and limits are counted in tokens.
OpenAI's newer API. Its replies can be a list of content blocks, which is why .content may be a list and .text is safer.
LangChain's tracing service. With LANGSMITH_TRACING=true and a key in .env, every run is recorded with no code changes.
A recorded run showing each step, its inputs and outputs, latency, tokens and cost.
A function an agent may call. The model sees only its name, input schema and description, and asks for it; the framework runs it.
An LLM that decides which tools to call, in a loop, until it can answer. Agent = LLM + tools.
Ask the model; if it requests a tool, run it and send back the result; repeat until it answers in plain text. Also called the ReAct loop.
A line starting with @ placed above a function to add behaviour. @tool turns a function into an agent tool.
Annotations like query: str that say what type a value should be. LangChain turns them into the tool's input schema.
The text in triple quotes at the top of a function. For a tool it's the description the model reads to decide when to call it.
A message typed by the user. An agent's input is a list of messages, starting with one of these.
The message LangChain adds after running a tool. It holds the tool's result, which the model reads next.
A web search API built for LLMs. Free tier: 1,000 credits a month. Its key must be named TAVILY_API_KEY.
Software development kit: a vendor's library for calling its service from code, such as TavilyClient.
A ready-made LangChain component published by a vendor, such as langchain_tavily.TavilySearch. Less code for you, kept up to date by them.
Making the model return data that matches a schema, instead of free text, so programs can use it without parsing.
A Python library for describing data shapes as classes (BaseModel) and validating that data fits them.
A simple text format for structured data: {curly braces} for objects, [square brackets] for lists. The common language of APIs.
